core.title: Keep the train registry and per-train documents mutually coherent
core.given: At CONFIRM, the corpus contains a train registry (profile: layout.registries#train_registry) and per-train documents at the per-train document location (profile: layout.locations#train_documents), whatever this plan changed.
core.then: Every train-registry row must name a path that resolves to an existing file anywhere on disk, and every per-train document at the per-train document location (profile: layout.locations#train_documents), other than registry sidecars (profile: layout.locations#train_document_sidecars), must be named by a registry row: no dangling rows, no orphan documents.
prefer: Plan a train's registry row and document as one change, both derived from its train_id.
Remove a train's row and document together.
Fix pre-existing dangling rows or orphan documents before confirming.
avoid: Writing a row before its document exists (dangling row): consumers resolve through it and some crash.
Leaving a document no row names (orphan document): inert, but residue of document-before-registry ordering.
Counting registry sidecars as per-train documents.
unless: Registry sidecars at the per-train document location (profile: layout.locations#train_document_sidecars) are not per-train documents, so they need no registry row.
core.why: Consumers resolve trains through the registry, so a row naming an absent file breaks them; unregistered documents are residue of document-before-registry ordering and must be reportable.
evidence: The corpus-wide train registry / per-train document coherence check passes at CONFIRM.
Each failure identifies the train, the direction (dangling row or orphan document), the registry value and the document value.
verification: Corpus-wide check at CONFIRM: evaluated over the whole corpus, not only artifacts touched by the current plan; pre-existing violations are findings, and any finding blocks confirmation.

Dangling direction: for each registry row, the named path must resolve to an existing file anywhere on disk, with no repository boundary; a target outside the repository is still checked, and a missing external target is still reported. The target location is not restricted to the per-train document location, and no sidecar exclusion applies to this direction.

Orphan direction: each per-train document at the per-train document location (profile: layout.locations#train_documents) must be named by some registry row; registry sidecars (profile: layout.locations#train_document_sidecars) are excluded from this enumeration only.
Each finding reports the train, the direction (dangling row or orphan document), the registry value and the document value.
Disposition strict: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline (severity 3); enforcement is confirm-blocking.
The check reports dangling rows as findings instead of crashing the way registry consumers do when they resolve a row to an absent file.
The check does not cover coherence inside the registry-sidecar trees; those are governed by their own rules.

values: dangling row (a registry row names a path that resolves to no file)
orphan document (no registry row names the document)

fires: At CONFIRM, any train-registry row names a path that does not resolve to an existing file, wherever that path points, inside or outside the repository.
At CONFIRM, a per-train document at the per-train document location (not a registry sidecar) is named by no registry row.
A dangling row or orphan document already existed before this plan, and the plan only edits unrelated content: confirmation still checks and reports it.
A plan adds, renames, moves or removes a train row or document without updating the other side.
doesNotFire: Orphan direction only: registry sidecars at the per-train document location are not enumerated as per-train documents needing a row; a registry row naming a missing sidecar path is still a dangling row.
A content-only edit to a train document when every row resolves and every document is registered (the corpus is coherent in both directions).
Coherence inside the registry-sidecar trees, which is governed by its own rules.

profileRequirements.meaning: Path of the registry artifact that enumerates every train (each row naming a train document path); its rows are the subjects of the dangling direction.

Location (glob) of the per-train document tree; the documents enumerated there (minus registry sidecars) are the subjects of the orphan direction, and the dangling direction's targets are deliberately not restricted to it.

Names or globs inside the per-train document tree that are registry sidecars (supporting artifacts), not per-train documents; they are excluded from the orphan enumeration only, never from the dangling direction.

neutralityNotes: The core keeps ATDD-method vocabulary shared across realizations (train, train_id, registry, planner, the CONFIRM phase) but names no stack artifact, path or suffix. All three concrete locations go through existing vocabulary v3 map keys as entries, so no new keys are proposed: the registry path is layout.registries#train_registry, the per-train document tree is layout.locations#train_documents (layout.plan_item stays what the vocabulary defines — the path pattern of a single plan artifact — and does not fit a whole document subtree), and the sidecar names are layout.locations#train_document_sidecars. The dangling direction deliberately has no repository boundary: a row's target is checked wherever it points, inside or outside the repository, and a missing external target is reported. The underscore-prefix sidecar marker is treated as profile data (the Bun value of layout.locations#train_document_sidecars), not as part of the obligation. Sibling-rule cross-references (planner.train.registry, planner.interlocking.registry-mirrors-document, planner.train.interlocking-home), the validator and finding ids, and the validation family/template/variant metadata stay bunOnly; their neutral content (two directions, sidecar exclusion scoped to the orphan direction only, whole-corpus confirm-blocking evaluation, strict disposition, failure-report shape) lives in core.verification.
